doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Solo space with James and the Jam Session short with Teddy Powell
summary: He stayed about a year and a half, got some trumpet features, and appeared in the band movie short Jam Session.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: The Pied Pipers, yeah. So when you were with Harry, for a couple of years?
Yeah. About a year and a half.
Did you start to want to get more solo space or were you happy just to—

Well I enjoyed listening to Harry so much, I admired him so much, I was happy to be in that band, because I learned a lot in that band. Because Harry said, he said, “Jack I know you played with Red Norvo you played solos” you know. And I said, “Yeah but that’s all right, don’t mind.” He says he thought I wouldn’t be happy, you know, not playing. But still and all at the end, when we got on location, when we got on location, at the end of the night like he’d take off maybe the last half hour, and I would play. We had some different songs that had trumpet solos, and not his solos, but trumpet solos where I would take off on.
Did you ever get involved on any of those band movies? Those short movies they did?

Yeah. I made one with Teddy Powell. I think the name, yes, I remember the name, “Jam Session.” It was a lot of bands. And I was with Teddy Powell. And I come out and I did a vocal I think, I’m not sure anymore. Yeah, Teddy Powell’s band.
We should get a copy of that.
The name of it is “Jam Session.”
That’s the name of the movie short or whatever, the band movie anyway.
Well it’s probably around, you’ll have to search I guess you know.
